GEN.name: General (non-hazardous) waste
GEN.handling: Only for genuinely uncontaminated items. If in doubt, do not default to this bin.
GEN.notes: If any doubt, choose UNK, not GEN.

REC.name: Dry recycling
REC.notes: Anything that touched samples or reagents is not recycling.

GLS.name: Clean glass
GLS.handling: Triple-rinse empty chemical bottles (rinsate goes to the correct liquid stream), deface labels. Broken glass goes in a rigid box, never a bag.
GLS.notes: Contaminated glass goes to a sharps category instead.

BIO-AUT.name: Biological solids - autoclave route
BIO-AUT.container: Autoclave bag in rigid bin (orange / per local scheme)
BIO-AUT.handling: Aspirate free liquid first. Bag loosely, add autoclave indicator tape, autoclave before disposal.
BIO-AUT.notes: Never add solvents, bleach, guanidinium, formaldehyde or cytotoxics.

BIO-GM.name: GM / transduced material - inactivate
BIO-GM.handling: Inactivate (validated autoclave cycle or chemical) before it leaves the lab. Viral vectors follow the containment-level SOP. Label as GM.
BIO-GM.notes: Follow the lab's GM risk assessment.

BIO-INC.name: Biological - incineration
BIO-INC.handling: Seal, label, hold for clinical waste collection.
BIO-INC.notes: Follow the institution's human tissue and clinical waste policy.

BIO-LIQ.name: Biological liquids
BIO-LIQ.handling: Inactivate with hypochlorite at the validated concentration and contact time in your SOP, then drain; or autoclave in a suitable vessel (never once bleach is added).
BIO-LIQ.notes: Hazardous additives (solvents, guanidinium, azide, cytotoxics) mean it is NOT this category.

SHP-INF.name: Sharps - biological
SHP-INF.handling: Do not recap or bend. Fill to the line only. Close and label when full.

SHP-CHEM.name: Sharps - chemical / fixative
SHP-CHEM.handling: As for biological sharps; write the contaminant on the label.
SHP-CHEM.notes: CMR-contaminated sharps: label clearly and notify the waste coordinator.

CHEM-NH.name: Non-halogenated solvents
CHEM-NH.handling: Keep halogenated solvents out. Vented cap, fume cupboard for decanting, list every constituent on the label.
CHEM-NH.notes: Never add oxidisers (bleach, nitric acid, peroxide).

CHEM-HAL.name: Halogenated solvents (incl. phenol-chloroform)
CHEM-HAL.handling: Fume cupboard. Keep separate from non-halogenated solvents (different disposal route).

CHEM-AQ.name: Hazardous aqueous
CHEM-AQ.handling: Collect, list all constituents, keep azide away from acids and metal.

CHEM-ACID.name: Acid waste
CHEM-ACID.handling: Keep apart from bases, bleach, azide, cyanides and organics.
CHEM-ACID.notes: Do not neutralise unless your SOP permits.

CHEM-BASE.name: Alkaline waste
CHEM-BASE.handling: Keep apart from acids and aluminium.
CHEM-BASE.notes: Do not neutralise unless your SOP permits.

CHEM-GUA.name: Guanidinium / phenol lysis waste
CHEM-GUA.container: Dedicated labelled carboy (not shared with bleach waste)
CHEM-GUA.handling: Own stream. Never bleach, never acidify, never autoclave.
CHEM-GUA.notes: Check the kit safety sheet for which buffers contain guanidinium.

CHEM-SOL.name: Chemically contaminated solids
CHEM-SOL.container: Rigid labelled chemical solid waste bin / double bag
CHEM-SOL.handling: Drain free liquid first. Never autoclave. Keep CMR items separate.

CMR-LIQ.name: CMR liquids (carcinogen / mutagen / reprotoxic)
CMR-LIQ.container: Sealed labelled bottle in secondary containment
CMR-LIQ.handling: Own stream. Never drain. Some sites require specific inactivation or filtration first.
CMR-LIQ.notes: Check the SDS for H340 / H350 / H360 hazard statements.

CMR-SOL.name: CMR solids
CMR-SOL.handling: Own stream. Never autoclave, never general waste.

CYT.name: Cytotoxic / cytostatic
CYT.handling: Never autoclave or bleach-and-drain. Purple stream for incineration.

RAD.name: Radioactive - OUT OF SCOPE
RAD.container: Do not dispose - refer to Radiation Protection Supervisor
RAD.handling: The tool must not classify this. Escalate.

DRAIN.name: Non-hazardous aqueous - drain with flush
DRAIN.handling: Small volumes only, roughly pH 6-10, run water before and after. Local trade-effluent rules apply.
DRAIN.notes: Any item flagged NO_DRAIN must never land here.

UNK.name: Unsure - escalate
UNK.container: Do not dispose - label and quarantine
UNK.handling: Ask the supervisor or safety officer. The tool defaults here when confidence is low.

SHP-CYT.name: Sharps - cytotoxic
SHP-CYT.handling: As for biological sharps; never mix with other sharps.

PHARM.name: Pharmaceutical (non-cytotoxic)
PHARM.handling: Keep in original packaging where possible. Never drain.
PHARM.notes: Controlled drugs follow a separate legal process - escalate.

REACT.name: Reactive / unstable chemicals
REACT.container: Own labelled container; vented cap if the site uses them
REACT.handling: Never combine with any other waste. Fume cupboard. Quench only under an approved SOP by trained staff.
REACT.notes: If crystals are visible or the container is old, do not move it - call the safety officer.

LABPACK.name: Surplus reagents (lab pack)
LABPACK.container: Original container, listed on the lab-pack inventory
LABPACK.handling: Do not decant or combine. Keep the label legible, list on the inventory, store by hazard class.
LABPACK.notes: Collected by the specialist contractor as a lab pack.

METAL.name: Heavy-metal waste
METAL.handling: Own stream. Never drain. Keep apart from azide.

TAKEBACK.name: Supplier take-back packaging
TAKEBACK.handling: Clean and dry; remove labels where required.
TAKEBACK.notes: Only where the supplier runs a scheme - otherwise recycling or general waste.

REUSE.name: Reuse / redistribute
REUSE.handling: Advertise to other labs before disposal; check expiry and storage conditions.
REUSE.notes: Not for opened, expired or unlabelled items.

WEEE.name: Electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE)
WEEE.handling: Decontaminate and tag as safe before collection.
WEEE.notes: Contact the estates or equipment team.

BATT.name: Batteries
BATT.handling: Tape the terminals of lithium cells. Do not bin.

CYL.name: Gas cylinders
CYL.container: Return to supplier / designated cylinder store
CYL.handling: Close valve, cap, label as empty or full, store upright and secured.

ANI.name: Animal waste - OUT OF SCOPE
ANI.container: Do not dispose - follow the animal facility procedure
ANI.handling: The tool must not classify this. Escalate.

HICON.name: High-containment pathogens - OUT OF SCOPE
HICON.container: Do not dispose - follow the containment facility procedure
HICON.handling: The tool must not classify this. Escalate.

items.name: Used gloves - no biological or chemical contact
items.steps: Remove without touching the outer surface.
items.do_not: Not if the gloves touched cell culture, reagents or lysates.

items.name: Bench roll / paper towels - uncontaminated
Wipes - clean surface, 70% ethanol only
items.do_not: Not if wiping up spills of anything other than ethanol.

items.name: Cardboard and paper packaging (kit boxes, sleeves)
Empty tip racks / plastic packaging - clean and unused
items.do_not: Not if it held used consumables.

items.name: Empty reagent bottles / clean glass (rinsed)
items.steps: Triple-rinse; send rinsate to the correct liquid stream; deface label; remove cap.
items.do_not: Do not bin unrinsed bottles that held hazardous chemicals.

items.name: Broken glass - uncontaminated (Pasteur pipettes, slides, coverslips)
items.steps: Rigid broken-glass box only, never a bag.

items.name: Cell culture flasks, plates and dishes (non-GM, media aspirated)
items.steps: Aspirate media into the biological liquid waste first; bag loosely; autoclave.
items.do_not: No bleach, solvents or cytotoxic-treated cells in this bag.

items.name: Serological pipettes (plastic) - cell culture
items.steps: Tip-down in a rigid pipette discard tub; autoclave the tub.
items.why: Biological contact with a puncture risk.

items.name: Pipette tips and microtubes - biological sample contact
items.do_not: Not if contaminated with solvents, guanidinium, CMR agents or cytotoxics.

items.name: Gloves - biological contact (cell culture, lysates)
Used cryovials (empty)
Aspirated media, PBS and trypsin washes (no hazardous additives)
items.steps: Inactivate with hypochlorite per your SOP then drain, or autoclave in a suitable vessel.
items.do_not: Do not add bleach if guanidinium, acid, formaldehyde, ammonium or solvents are present. Do not autoclave after bleach is added.

items.name: Transfected / virally transduced cell waste (solids and liquids)
items.steps: Inactivate before it leaves the lab; vectors follow the containment-level SOP; label as GM.
items.do_not: Do not mix with non-GM waste if policy requires separation.

items.name: Cell culture waste from cytotoxic drug treatment
items.why: Cytotoxic exposure overrides the biological route.

items.name: Human / animal tissue, FFPE blocks, unfixed samples
items.steps: Seal, label, hold for clinical waste collection.

items.name: Needles and syringes (biological)
items.steps: Do not recap or bend; fill to the line only.

items.name: Scalpel / razor blades
items.do_not: Not if contaminated with CMR agents (see sharps - chemical).

items.name: Broken glass or slides contaminated with biological material
items.steps: Sharps bin, not a glass box.

items.name: Sharps contaminated with chemicals (e.g. EtBr gel-cutting blades, stain-contaminated glass)
items.steps: Write the contaminant on the label.
items.why: Chemical contamination needs the chemical sharps stream.

items.name: Polyacrylamide gels (after SDS-PAGE)
items.why: Local lab policy: protein gels and blot membranes go to the autoclave route.

items.name: Unpolymerised acrylamide / bis-acrylamide solution or powder
items.steps: Powder handled in a fume cupboard; double glove.

items.name: SDS-PAGE running buffer (Tris-glycine-SDS)
items.do_not: Not if it contains azide or other additives.

items.name: Western transfer buffer (contains methanol)
items.why: Methanol content; some sites allow small volumes via drain.

items.name: TBS-T / PBS-T wash buffers (no azide)
Buffers containing sodium azide (antibody diluent, storage buffers)
items.do_not: No acids (hydrazoic acid gas). Never drain: azide forms explosive metal azides in plumbing.

items.name: Western blot membranes (PVDF / nitrocellulose) after imaging
items.why: Local lab policy: protein gels and blot membranes go to the autoclave route.

items.name: ECL / chemiluminescent substrate (used)
Coomassie stain / destain (methanol-acetic acid)
items.why: Flammable with acid content; some sites split acidic fractions.

items.name: RIPA / detergent lysis buffer with lysate (no guanidinium)
items.do_not: Not for guanidinium buffers (see lysis waste).

items.name: Agarose gels stained with ethidium bromide
TAE / TBE buffer containing ethidium bromide
items.steps: Some sites filter through charcoal first.

items.name: Gloves, tips and paper contaminated with EtBr, DAB or other CMR agents
Agarose gels with SYBR Safe / GelRed / similar stains
items.why: Marketed as safer but disposal advice varies by site.

items.name: TAE / TBE buffer (no stain)
PCR / qPCR tubes, plates and tips with DNA template
items.steps: Autoclave route (some sites allow general waste if non-GM and no human material).
items.do_not: Treat as GM waste if template is recombinant.

items.name: TRIzol / TRI Reagent organic phase (phenol-chloroform)
items.steps: Glass or solvent-resistant container; fume cupboard.

items.name: TRIzol / TRI Reagent aqueous phase and lysate waste
Column-kit flow-through and buffers with guanidinium (lysis / binding)
items.steps: Check the kit safety sheet for guanidinium buffers.

items.name: Spin columns, collection tubes and tips from extraction kits
Ethanol / isopropanol waste (precipitation, washes)
Chloroform (waste)
Phenol / buffer-saturated phenol (waste)
items.why: Toxic and corrosive; many sites collect separately.

items.name: Urea / ammonium bicarbonate digestion buffers
items.why: Ammonium and urea react with hypochlorite.

items.name: Iodoacetamide / DTT / TCEP reduction-alkylation waste
Acetonitrile / water LC-MS waste (with formic acid or TFA)
items.steps: If TFA is present, check whether your site treats it as halogenated.

items.name: Trifluoroacetic acid / neat formic acid
C18 StageTips, desalting tips / columns, SP3 bead tubes
LC-MS autosampler vials (glass, solvent residue)
Cell-surface biotinylation reagents and quench
items.why: Reactive reagent with biological origin; collect conservatively.

items.name: Streptavidin / magnetic beads after pull-down
items.why: Lysate and chemical residue; policy varies.

items.name: Peptide digests / leftover protein samples
MTT reagent and solubilised formazan (DMSO or acidified isopropanol)
96-well plates after MTT solubilisation
Assay plates (CellTiter-Glo, resazurin) with lysed or live cells
items.do_not: Not if cells were drug-treated with cytotoxics.

items.name: Trypan blue solution
items.why: Carries a carcinogen classification in some jurisdictions; check the SDS.

items.name: Cell counting slides / coverslips with trypan blue
Formaldehyde / formalin / 4% PFA solutions
Xylene / xylene substitutes
DAB (diaminobenzidine) solutions and DAB-stained consumables
items.steps: Some sites inactivate per SOP before collection.

items.name: Stained slides and coverslips (fixed tissue / cells, mounting medium)
Mounting medium (with or without DAPI) residues and tips
Antibody solutions in PBS (azide-free), blocking buffers
items.do_not: If azide is present use the azide item.

items.name: Strong acids (HCl, H2SO4, HNO3)
items.do_not: No bleach, azide, cyanide or organics.

items.name: Strong alkali (NaOH / KOH, roughly pH 11 and above)
Used bleach / hypochlorite decontamination solution
items.do_not: Never combine with acids, ammonia/ammonium, guanidinium, formaldehyde or solvents. Never autoclave.
items.why: Oxidiser; releases toxic gas with many lab chemicals.

items.name: Radiolabelled material (32P, 3H, 125I, etc.)
items.steps: Escalate to the Radiation Protection Supervisor.
items.do_not: Do not classify in this tool.

items.name: Unlabelled / unidentified liquid or container
Acetic anhydride (waste or surplus)
items.steps: Own labelled container with vented cap; fume cupboard; quench only under an approved SOP.
items.do_not: Not in the solvent carboy, aqueous waste or the drain. Keep from alcohols, amines, bases and oxidisers. Check site record-keeping rules for controlled drug precursors.
items.why: Reacts exothermically with water and alcohols.

items.name: Peroxide-forming solvents past date (diethyl ether, THF, dioxane)
items.steps: Do not open if crystals are visible or the container is old; call the safety officer.
items.do_not: Do not pour into the solvent carboy.
items.why: Peroxides can detonate on friction or heat.

items.name: Picric acid (dry or old)
items.steps: Do not move or open; call the safety officer.
items.do_not: Never let it dry out; never touch a crusted lid.

items.name: Sodium azide powder or solids
items.steps: Own container; keep dry and away from acids and metals.
items.do_not: No acids. No metal containers or drains.
items.why: Toxic; forms explosive azides with metals.

items.name: Needles, syringes and glass used with cytotoxic drugs
items.steps: Purple-lidded sharps bin; fill to the line only.
items.do_not: Never in orange or yellow sharps bins.

items.name: Expired or unused non-cytotoxic medicines (including veterinary)
Solutions or solids with heavy metals (Hg, Cd, Pb, Cr(VI))
items.do_not: Never drain. Keep apart from azide.

items.name: Silver stain solutions (silver nitrate) from gel staining
items.steps: Collect all silver steps; do not drain.
items.do_not: No organics or solvents. Never drain.
items.why: Silver is a toxic metal and silver nitrate is an oxidiser.

items.name: Surplus or unwanted reagents in original containers
items.steps: Keep original container and label; list on the lab-pack inventory.
items.why: Unknown mixtures are riskier than labelled originals.

items.name: Polystyrene boxes, clean cool packs and supplier packaging
items.steps: Clean and dry; return where the supplier offers take-back.
items.why: Supplier schemes exist for some items.

items.name: Unopened in-date surplus reagents and consumables
items.do_not: Not if opened, expired or unlabelled.

items.name: Old electronic equipment (plate readers, power supplies)
Batteries (instrument, pipette controllers)
items.steps: Tape the terminals of lithium cells.

items.name: UV bulbs, fluorescent tubes, transilluminator lamps
items.do_not: Not in general waste or glass.

items.name: Gas cylinders (empty or unwanted)
items.steps: Close valve, cap, label empty or full.

items.name: Animal carcasses, bedding and in-vivo waste
items.do_not: Do not classify in this tool.

items.name: Pathogens above containment level 2
items.do_not: Do not classify in this tool.

incompatibilities.rule: Block: never place in the same container or treat together.

incompatibilities.hazard: Forms toxic chloramine vapours (includes ammonium salts and urea)
Releases toxic gases when guanidinium salts meet hypochlorite
incompatibilities.rule: Block. Do not use bleach on lysis-buffer waste.

incompatibilities.hazard: Reactive and toxic chlorinated by-products (e.g. with acetone or alcohols)
incompatibilities.rule: Block. Do not add bleach to solvent-containing waste.

incompatibilities.hazard: Forms hydrazoic acid, a toxic and explosive gas

incompatibilities.rule: Block unless a neutralisation SOP applies.

incompatibilities.hazard: Different disposal routes; mixing raises cost and risk
Cytotoxic waste must stay in its own stream
CMR agents must not enter general chemical, biological or drain streams
incompatibilities.rule: Block mixing with anything outside CMR streams.

incompatibilities.hazard: Reacts violently or exothermically with water, alcohols and many other wastes
incompatibilities.rule: Block mixing with anything; own container.

incompatibilities.hazard: Peroxides can detonate on contact with other waste or when disturbed
incompatibilities.rule: Block mixing; escalate to the safety officer.
